First, let $u=4-7x.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-7\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{7}\,\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{8}{4-7x}\,\text{d}x & =8\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{7}\,\text{d}u\right) \\ & =-\frac{8}{7}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ & =-\frac{8}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\ & =-\frac{8}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡|4-7x|+C\end{aligned}
$$
